title: Kimchi Fried Rice
subtitle: Korean rice stir-fried with fermented cabbage and pork belly
excerpt: Day-old rice stir-fried with kimchi, pork belly, and gochujang until the rice is crispy and deeply flavoured. Topped with a fried egg and a drizzle of sesame oil.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kimchi fried rice (kimchi bokkeumbap) is a Korean home-cooking staple, made from leftover rice and the kimchi that is a constant presence in Korean fridges. Like most fried rice dishes across East Asia, it is a practical dish built around what is available rather than a recipe requiring specific ingredients. The sour, fermented flavour of older kimchi is actually preferred for cooking over fresh kimchi, as it contributes more depth to the dish. Using freshly made kimchi produces a milder, less complex flavour.

recipeTools.notes: Or a large frying pan over the highest heat available.

content.text: Day-old cold rice is essential: freshly cooked rice is too moist and will steam instead of fry, producing clumpy results. Spread freshly cooked rice on a tray and refrigerate overnight to dry it out. The wok should be very hot before anything goes in: the brief, high-heat fry is what gives the rice its slight crispiness and the smoky flavour known as wok hei.

items.preparation: cooked the day before and refrigerated
fermented kimchi, roughly chopped — buy from an Asian supermarket or Korean grocery
sliced, white and green parts separated

content.text: Heat the wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the vegetable oil. Add the pork belly and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through and beginning to crisp. Add the white parts of the spring onion and garlic. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.

Add the kimchi and gochujang. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until the kimchi starts to caramelise slightly. Add the cold rice and break up any clumps. Stir-fry over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the rice is heated through and beginning to crisp at the edges. Add the soy sauce and stir through.
Drizzle the sesame oil over the rice and toss through. Divide between bowls. Fry the eggs separately and place on top. Scatter with green spring onion tops, sesame seeds, and crumbled nori if using.
